Quick start

  1. Double-click a wall or door (as the GM).
  2. Switch to the Threshold tab and pick a barrier profile, e.g. “Gate (bars)”, “Window” or “Glass door”.
  3. Click Update Wall. Done: the wall now has movement, vision, light, sound, door and texture set up.

A profile is a starting point: change any setting for this one wall. Setting the profile back to None and saving restores the wall's original settings.

The Threshold tab

At the top: profile, door control, state and the state matrix. Colours: red blocks, yellow partly, green lets through. Click a column to edit that state.

Below are collapsible sections:

  • What gets through: values for the closed state, separately for movement, vision, light, sound, cover and projectiles.
  • Opening ajar (doors only): see “Opening doors ajar”.
  • Behaviour in other states: see “States”.
  • Appearance: texture and animation.
  • Material and interaction: material, durability, whether players can operate the barrier.

While a profile is active, the native movement, sight, light, sound and door fields on the Wall tab are locked: Threshold controls them.

Proximity and ranges

A channel set to Proximity lets sight, light or sound through only when the source is close to the barrier. That is how a window works (you see through it up close), and how listening at a door works.

Ranges are in grid squares, not feet or metres, so profiles fit any system. The value in scene units is shown below the field, e.g. “= 5 ft”. Note: 60 squares is 300 feet, practically the whole map.

States

A barrier can be closed, open, ajar, locked or damaged. Ajar and locked apply to doors only.

  • Without overrides an open barrier lets everything through, and locked or damaged behave like closed.
  • Change that per channel in Behaviour in other states. “Default (…)” shows what the built-in rule gives.
  • Each state can also have its own texture: a broken window, a smashed barricade, curtains drawn back.

Players open and close doors with Foundry's usual door icon; the module updates the state itself.

Opening doors ajar

Preset doors use physical opening: when ajar, the leaf really swings on its hinge (sliding doors retract into the frame), and Foundry works out what can be seen through the gap.

  • From the map: hold Alt and scroll over the door icon. Up: wider, down: push to. At 0 the door closes.
  • On the tab: opening slider, hinge, direction and a live schematic.
  • While the gap is narrower than the threshold (default 1 square), a helper wall in the frame blocks movement only. The module creates and removes it; don't edit it.
  • Clicking the icon of a door that is ajar opens it fully; clicking again closes it.

If a door swings on the wrong end, switch Hinge to the other end. If it swings the wrong way, change Swings.

Durability and damage

Destructible barriers get durability from their material (wood 30, glass 15…). A bar is shown under them on the map; module settings choose who sees it.

Select the wall and use a macro:

const thr = game.modules.get("threshold").api;
await thr.damage(12);   // damage
await thr.repair();     // full repair

At 0 the barrier becomes Damaged: a broken door or barricade can be walked through, a window is smashed. Repairing returns it to Closed.

Appearance and textures

In Appearance pick one of the 16 bundled textures or any image of your own with the browse button.

  • Doors use Foundry's animated doors: the texture swings, slides, rises or descends when opening.
  • Other barriers (bars, windows, force field, barricade) are drawn by the module, below tokens and above tiles; fog of war hides them like tiles.
  • Thickness is in grid squares; thin by default so the barrier doesn't cover the map.

Module settings

  • Apply profiles to native walls: off means profiles are stored as data only.
  • Durability bars on the map: nobody, GM only, or GM and players.
  • Threshold guide: opens this window.
  • Show the welcome window after updates: a per-user setting.

For players

  • Open and close doors as usual by clicking their icon.
  • Hold Alt and scroll over a door icon to open it a crack or push it to. This works if the GM lets players use that door and it isn't locked.
  • Through a door ajar you see only what can really be seen through the gap. You can't squeeze through a narrow gap.
  • You see more through a window when you stand close to it. Sometimes you can hear what's behind a door.

Macros and API

const thr = game.modules.get("threshold").api;
await thr.apply("gate");          // profile for the selected walls
await thr.ajar(0.33);             // stand the selected door ajar (~30°)
await thr.damage(10);             // damage
await thr.repair();               // repair
thr.profiles.list();              // list profiles
thr.guide();                      // this window

System modules can add profiles with the threshold.registerProfiles hook and change damage with threshold.preDamage.

Troubleshooting

  • I can see through a wall from across the map: check the proximity range; it is in grid squares.
  • A door swings on the wrong end or the wrong way: change Hinge or Swings in Opening ajar.
  • I can't edit movement and sight on the Wall tab: the profile controls them; change them on the Threshold tab or set the profile to None.
  • Alt + wheel zooms instead of opening: point exactly at the door icon; report it if that doesn't help.
  • Something doesn't work: open the console (F12), copy the messages with “[THR]” and report them in the repository.
